clue.text: In season, show egg dropped from chicken outlet

indicators.note: the egg is let fall out of the chicken, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a poussin is a very young chicken raised for eating
an egg is O-shaped, so O stands for it
Boots is a British chain of chemist shops, a retail outlet

explanation.surface: A poultry shop seems to have mislaid an egg from its chicken, though the clue opens by hinting at a seasonal show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped from' removes the O from POUSSIN to leave PUSSIN; BOOTS is the high-street chemist chain. The show is a Christmas pantomime, hence 'in season'.
explanation.definitionFit: This fairy tale is a staple British pantomime, staged around Christmas, so it is a seasonal show.

clue.text: Having a butcher's backing to trade in city, as it were

indicators.note: the picked letter goes into the city's name

parts.note: Peking is the old name for Beijing; 'as it were' flags that the name is not the current one

indicators.note: the back of the word trade is its final letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: Someone backs a trade deal in a city, after a quick look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so having a butcher's is looking. The final E of 'trade' slots into PEKING.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a butcher's is a look, so having one means taking a sly look.

clue.text: Crack part of shoe, squeezing number of toes within?

indicators.note: the shoe part holds another piece tightly inside it

parts.note: the sole is the underside of a shoe
a foot has five toes inside the shoe; V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A cracked shoe sole pinches the toes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to solve it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Rogue sea's churning, negotiating past it will be difficult

definitions.text: negotiating past it will be difficult

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue

indicators.note: a churning sea is stirred up, so the letters of sea's are mixed

explanation.surface: A rogue sea is churning, so any ship trying to get past will struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or blockage is something you cannot get beyond, hence a dead end that is hard to pass.

clue.text: Subversive soon obstructing kid upset evening

indicators.note: the rearranged word blocks the middle of the other piece by sitting inside it
in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: to kid is to rib, tease

indicators.note: subversive means overturning, so the letters of soon are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel's plan to cause trouble soon ruins a child's evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' is not a time of day here but a greeting, as in 'Evening!', which the French say as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French greeting means good evening, so 'evening' used as a greeting matches it.

clue.text: Official award on day collected by holiday worker?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: the day is picked up and held inside the worker

parts.note: a busman's holiday is leisure time spent doing one's usual work

explanation.surface: An official is given an award on the day a bus driver on holiday picks it up.
explanation.walkthrough: A busman's holiday is a British idiom for a break spent doing much the same as your job, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate complaints against organisations.

clue.text: Don's OK with shelter, assuming no charge for mum

parts.note: a don is a Spanish gentleman, and Spanish for yes is si

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the shelter takes the abbreviation inside

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A university don is happy to shelter someone without charging his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like an Oxbridge tutor, but it is a Spanish title, giving the Spanish yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as in 'keep mum' means saying nothing, so the noun for quiet fits it.

clue.text: Common ground where picnic served

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an area shared by two things
second meaning: split as ..., the food is served on your lap

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words, telling you a picnic plate rests over your lap.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two areas share part of their extent they coincide, which is common ground.

clue.text: Some of military issue boots repelling one actor

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: the boots push the one away, so it is removed

parts.note: wellies are wellington boots
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Soldiers' standard-issue boots fend off something, and one actor appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repelling one' drops the I from WELLIES (rubber boots in British English) to leave WELLES.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the American actor and director best known for Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Bees occupying river's course?

indicators.note: the bees take up residence inside the river's name

parts.note: the Nile with its possessive s
B twice, two letters called bee

explanation.surface: Bees have taken over the course of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River's course' reads as the path of a river, but 'course' is a part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small snacks served before a meal could loosely count as a course, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Team supporter's first getting pasty, then the drink and the smoke

indicators.note: supporter's first means just the opening letter of that word

parts.note: its first letter is S
pasty and wan both mean pale
the drink is informal for the sea
the Smoke is a nickname for London, whose financial district is the City

explanation.surface: A football fan starts the day with a pasty, then a drink and a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like a pastry but means pale. 'The Smoke' is British slang for London, and the City is its financial heart.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Welsh football club, known as the Swans.

clue.text: Appropriate age of school-leaver in France?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take for oneself, a verb
second meaning: French for sixteen, the age at which compulsory schooling ends

explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb to take. The second half wants a French number.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab something for yourself is to take it over, the verb sense of appropriate.

clue.text: Dazzling green light, reached son around highland area

indicators.note: turned around, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I
a nod is a sign of approval, like a green light
won as in reached a place, attained it
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A traffic light shines a bright green as a son arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, and setters often write it with the figure read as the letter I; 'around' turns the whole string, not just the son.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mountainous national park in north Wales, a highland region.

clue.text: Kit for dropping off on one's doorstep before match

parts.note: on your doorstep means very near, nigh
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Kit needed for a match turns up on someone's doorstep beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' sounds like a delivery but means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is clothing worn in bed, so outfit for going to sleep.

clue.text: Whiskey doctor picked up in sample vessel

indicators.note: these pieces go into the sample

parts.note: to taste is to sample, so a taster is a small sample
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A doctor collects a sample of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reverses MO to OM; W and OM go into TASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship with two masts is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Feed digitally, scoffing exotic lime without rind?

indicators.note: scoffing means eating, so the feed takes the other letters inside

parts.note: RSS is a web feed format

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of lime are rearranged

explanation.surface: An online feed eats exotic lime with no peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feed digitally' is the web-feed format, not eating; the question mark warns that rimless glasses are only fancifully rindless.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim is an outer edge, and rind is an outer layer, so having no rim is fancifully lacking rind.

clue.text: Force member to enter flower that's burst out

indicators.note: the policeman goes inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Exe is in Devon
plod is British slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A police officer pushes into a flower that has burst into bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Exe in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up is to burst out violently, the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Strip round the bend below exercise area

indicators.note: in a down clue, the last piece sits under the others

parts.note: PE is physical education
round the bend means mad, nuts

explanation.surface: A road strip loops round a bend beneath an exercise yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is the long-running comic strip by Charles Schulz featuring Charlie Brown.

clue.text: Large shops commoner in heart of age-old coastal inlet

indicators.note: the MP goes between the middle letters
the heart of age-old is its central pair of letters

parts.note: its middle letters are E and O
an MP sits in the House of Commons
a ria is a drowned river valley forming an inlet

explanation.surface: A commoner wanders into the heart of an ancient coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a big store or trading centre.

clue.text: Harry recalled stag flaunting musical style

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to harry is to nag

indicators.note: flaunting means displaying showily, so stag is jumbled

explanation.surface: Harry remembers a stag party where a musical style was shown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns NAG into GAN; 'flaunting' reorders STAG as GSTA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the hip-hop genre about gang life, so a kind of rap music.

clue.text: Devotee reportedly cultivated green veg

indicators.note: as reported in speech, so the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: cultivated means grew, as a crop; a pea is a green vegetable

explanation.surface: A keen gardener is said to have grown green vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A groupie is a fan who follows a band, an ardent follower.

clue.text: It has rocky faces overlooking lakes

definitions.text: It has rocky faces overlooking lakes

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the lakes
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of faces are shaken up

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A mountain with craggy faces looks down on lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: Scafell is a peak in England's Lake District, so it does overlook lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cumbrian mountain, neighbour of Scafell Pike, has crags rising above the Lake District's waters.

clue.text: Dog disrupted shop, alas eating article

indicators.note: the jumbled letters swallow the article
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of shop and alas are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dog has run amok in a shop, alas, and eaten an item.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small long-haired Tibetan breed, a kind of dog.

clue.text: Ducats periodically used in TV programme? As if!

indicators.note: the picked letters are put inside the programme

parts.note: QI is a British TV quiz show

indicators.note: taken at regular intervals, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: its even letters are U, A, S

explanation.surface: Ducats feature now and then in a television programme, which the speaker scoffs at.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a long-running British panel quiz hosted first by Stephen Fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasi means seemingly or as though, which matches 'as if' as a prefix sense.

clue.text: Ration books team uncovered outside

indicators.note: the trimmed team sits outside the books
with its cover taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a squad is a team
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A team rations its books, leaving them out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is a fixed share or allowance, as a ration is.

clue.text: When back, hound in Stratford given walk?

indicators.note: turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: Stratford is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the H

parts.note: a hunter, a hound used in hunting

explanation.surface: Back home in Stratford, a dog is taken for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Stratford suggests Shakespeare's town, but here it is Stratford in east London, where a Cockney says 'unter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll in a leisurely way is to take a gentle walk.

clue.text: Race for millennials?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Generation Y is another name for millennials

explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a contest, but it is the line of descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Race in the sense of offspring or descendants of a family line is one's offspring.

clue.text: Browse one array of chain letters etc

parts.note: to surf the web is to browse
an ace counts as one in cards
chain mail is armour made of linked rings

explanation.surface: Someone browses one long series of chain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Post sent by land or sea rather than by air covers letters and parcels.
